$comment: The state transitions of one item (a ticket) through the human pipeline, as the code and prompts implement them today. Each transition names the ACTOR that causes it, the SKILL that does the work, the MARKER that records it, and WHERE it is implemented. Topology is name/src/dst only; every other field is annotation.
item: a ticket, from filing to merged

actors.user: a person, via a board gesture (drag, button) or a CLI command
actors.daemon: the host process — it launches agents, posts their started markers, and is the only thing with push credentials
actors.skill: an agent running in a container, following the named prompt

unclassified_markers.doc: Posted by the pipeline but deliberately not transitions: they record content or decorate the card, and the item's state is unchanged by them.

states.name: filed
states.doc: The ticket exists. No pipeline activity.
states.holds: The ticket is open and carries no pipeline marker.
states.stale_when: Never. Waiting is what Backlog is for, and an item may rest here indefinitely.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. The machine does not start work nobody asked for. A person may hand a Backlog ticket straight to an agent — a directly invoked plan or ticket-review run posts its markers here without the board dispatching anything — but nothing begins on its own.

states.name: ticket-review
states.doc: The pre-planning gate is judging whether solving this ticket solves the problem.
states.holds: The pre-planning gate is running as the FIRST PHASE of the planning dispatch, so the agent that owns it is registered under the planning stage, not this one.
states.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace with no live agent, like any running stage.
states.if_nothing_happens: The agent's death is recorded as a PLANNING failure, because planning is the stage it runs under. Note the gap: the backlog stage has no *-failed marker of its own (failedHeaderFor returns none for it), so neither the live watcher nor the durable pass can red a card derived at backlog/running directly — recovery here depends entirely on the enclosing planning dispatch.

states.name: ticket-reviewed
states.doc: The gate returned a verdict: ready, reframed, superseded, escalated or rejected. The last three are stop decisions.
states.holds: A verdict is recorded with one of five heads.
states.stale_when: Never — a verdict is a resting point, not work in progress.
states.if_nothing_happens: For `ready` and `reframed`, the same run continues into planning without anything further. For the three stop heads the item rests in Backlog with the reason on the ticket; only a person restarts it.

states.name: planning
states.doc: A planner is exploring the codebase and writing an implementation plan.
states.holds: A planner owns the stage and [human:planning-started] is the item's newest planning marker.

states.name: planned
states.doc: A plan is attached to the ticket. The item waits for a human to start the build.
states.holds: A [human:plan] comment is attached and no build has started.
states.stale_when: Never. A plan nobody has acted on is not a fault.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. The machine does not begin an implementation on its own — a plan waits for a person to start the build.

states.name: nothing-to-do
states.doc: The planner proved the work is already merged. Clean terminal.
states.holds: The planner established the work is already merged. Clean terminal.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. The machine must never re-run its own clean terminal, which is exactly why reopen is a separate entry point from every retry gesture: the automatic relaunch drives the identical same-stage request.

states.name: preflight
states.doc: The fix run is resolving what it may do and settling what the evidence can settle, before any work.
states.holds: A fix run owns the implementation stage and is resolving what it may do before any work.

states.name: triaging
states.doc: The run is reproducing the report to reach a verdict.
states.holds: The run is reproducing the report; the implementation stage is claimed.

states.name: challenging
states.doc: A skeptic is trying to refute a not-a-bug or undetermined verdict before it is acted on.
states.holds: A skeptic is trying to refute a not-a-bug or undetermined verdict. It runs ONCE — a verdict that survives is not re-challenged.

states.name: resolved-no-fix
states.doc: The no-fix verdict survived the challenge. Clean terminal — the ticket needs no code change.
states.holds: The no-fix verdict survived the challenge. Clean terminal — no code change is warranted.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. As with nothing-to-do, only an explicitly human call may re-run a clean terminal.

states.name: fix-planning
states.doc: The self-planning fix run is producing its own plan.
states.holds: The self-planning fix run is writing its own plan, because it entered from a report rather than from a planned ticket.

states.name: fixing
states.doc: A regression test that fails first, then the change that makes it pass.
states.holds: A regression test that fails first exists, or is being written, along with the change that makes it pass.

states.name: verifying
states.doc: Proving the test fails before and passes after, on a green suite.
states.holds: The fix exists and its fails-before/passes-after evidence is being produced by something other than the code that wrote it.
states.note: This is the state SC-1136 froze in: a NOT DONE verify that halted silently left a card reading "being fixed" forever, which is the dead end the durable pass exists to close.

states.name: implementing
states.doc: A plan executor is carrying out an attached plan (the non-bug path).
states.holds: A plan executor is carrying out an ATTACHED plan. A launch onto a ticket with no plan is refused before any agent claims the stage.

states.name: handed-off
states.doc: Branch and commits are recorded on the ticket, checked reachable.
states.holds: Branch and commits are recorded on the ticket AND the commits were verified reachable on the branch before the marker was posted.
states.stale_when: The review was never chained — the live hook was lost to a daemon restart.
states.if_nothing_happens: reconcileOrphanedHandoffs chains the review, but only when the commits are DEFINITELY present on this machine. A clean absence or an unreadable check leaves the card alone rather than redding work another machine may be able to serve.

states.name: in-review
states.doc: A reviewer is checking the change against the ticket's acceptance criteria. In a board fix run this happens inline, in the same warm container.
states.holds: A reviewer owns the verification stage and is checking the change against the ticket's acceptance criteria.

states.name: reviewed
states.doc: The review returned a verdict. A failing verdict blocks the deploy and sends the item back to be rebuilt.
states.holds: A verdict is recorded. The board reads the daemon's blocking DECISION, never the verdict string.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing automatic on the shipping path: a passing verdict waits for the Deploy gesture, and a failing or incomplete one waits for a rework the board must offer, because the daemon refuses the deploy drop. The daemon does act here on the legacy PR path only.

states.name: deploying
states.doc: The daemon pushed the branch and opened a draft pull request.
states.holds: The branch is pushed and a DRAFT pull request is open, so a half-reviewed change is not mergeable by anyone.

states.name: pr-review
states.doc: The machine reviewer is reading the open pull request.
states.holds: The machine reviewer is reading the open pull request; the newest done-stage marker is a loop-started marker.

states.name: pr-fix
states.doc: The machine fixer is addressing the review's findings on the local branch.
states.holds: The machine fixer is committing to the LOCAL branch and never pushing, so the reviewer reads the new commit rather than a stale pushed head.

states.name: ci-gate
states.doc: Every check must be green before the merge.
states.holds: The review converged and every check must be green before the merge. If the base moved on, the branch is rebased and CI re-gated on the new head first.

states.name: deploy-fixing
states.doc: A CI failure or a rebase conflict dispatched the deploy fixer instead of failing the item.
states.holds: A mechanical failure — red CI or a rebase conflict — dispatched the fixer instead of failing the item. The fixer's container holds no push credentials.
states.note: Rounds are separately bounded by DefaultDeployFixRounds (2); past that the escalation names the condition that is blocking rather than advising a retry that would hit the same wall.

states.name: merged
states.doc: Merged, branch deleted, ticket closed. The shipping terminal.
states.holds: Merged, branch deleted, ticket closed. Past the merge, cleanup and closing are best-effort and never fail the item.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. This is the shipping terminal — the only state with no actor able to leave it.

states.name: awaiting-decision
states.doc: The item is parked on a genuine fork. Only a human choosing an answer moves it.

board.note: Idle in whatever column the card was in, with an open [human:options] block — pauseOnOpenOptions turns running or failed into idle. "Decision needed" is not a BoardState; the open block is what distinguishes it.

states.holds: An open [human:options] block names this item's own stage, or an earlier stage the answer would rework.
states.stale_when: Never by time. A pause on an open decision is deliberate, and BOTH the live guard (stagePausedOnOptions) and the reconcile pass exclude it from the stuck-running sweep on purpose — a card waiting for a person is not a card that has hung.
states.if_nothing_happens: Nothing. This is the one state the machine may not resolve for itself, which is the whole point of raising a fork rather than guessing.

states.name: stopped
states.doc: A stage gave up and said why: a spent budget, an unreviewable change, a failed deploy. Needs a human.
states.holds: A stage gave up and the marker says why, naming the blocking condition rather than offering a gesture that cannot work.
states.stale_when: Never automatically — a stop is a request for a person.
states.if_nothing_happens: Not nothing — this is the state most easily mistaken for a dead end. Within DefaultStageRetries (2) the machine relaunches the failed stage IN PLACE: the failure is recorded first and the relaunch is the same transition a person Retry gesture issues, so every existing guard applies unchanged. Past the budget it waits for a person. One further case clears it without any relaunch: a done-stage failure whose pull request the forge reports MERGED is retired by reconcileShippedFailures with a [human:deployed] marker, because the work shipped out of band and the red is stale rather than true.

states.name: substrate-down
states.doc: A stage reported the thing it needs was unreachable. Not a failure — it spends no retry budget and is relaunched when the substrate returns.
states.holds: A stage reported the thing it needs was unreachable. Nothing about the work is wrong, so it spends no retry budget.
states.stale_when: The outage has lasted past OutageWaitBound (6 hours). An outage that never ends looks exactly like one that will return, until someone measures how long it has run.
states.if_nothing_happens: Each reconcile tick relaunches the stage WITHOUT charging DefaultStageRetries, until the substrate returns and a *-started marker supersedes the outage. Past OutageWaitBound the card is handed to a person instead — still charging nothing.

states.name: unknown
states.doc: The item's own state is unchanged, but the tracker that carries it failed to load, so nothing can be observed about it. It is the only state not derived from the item's markers — it says the board could not look, not that the item moved. Every item on that tracker enters and leaves it together, and it resolves by itself on the next fetch that reads the source.

board.note: Not a placement at all. A card whose thread could not be read is marked Degraded and keeps its last-known stage and state, so the board shows an error banner rather than moving it anywhere.

states.holds: Nothing about the ITEM is known. Its own state is unchanged; the tracker carrying it failed to load, so every item on that tracker enters and leaves this state together.
states.stale_when: Not applicable — this is a property of the fetch, not of the item.
states.if_nothing_happens: The next fetch that reads the source re-derives the item's real state from its markers. It returns to whatever they say, not to where it started.

events.name: start-ticket-review
events.where: cmd/cmdplan — /human-ticket-review invoked directly against a Backlog ticket
events.doc: The pre-planning gate, run on its own: before any code is planned, something asks whether solving this ticket solves the problem.
events.prompt: human-ticket-reviewer-agent.md — the gate posts its own ticket-review-started marker

events.name: ticket-review-verdict
events.doc: The gate returned one of five heads. `ready` and `reframed` continue into planning; `superseded`, `escalated` and `rejected` are stop decisions and say why, so the item rests in Backlog with the reason on the ticket rather than quietly never being picked up.

events.name: start-planning
events.where: board_transition.go launchForwardStage / isPlanningRetry
events.doc: A drop on Planning. From planned it is a replan; from stopped or substrate-down it is a retry in place.

events.name: plan-attached
events.doc: The plan itself is attached as a [human:plan] comment; plan-ready is what moves the item. Planning run on its own attaches a plan to a ticket the board never dispatched, so the marker arrives with no planning-started before it.
events.where: internal/claude/embed/human-plan-skill.md posts plan-ready as its last step, whether or not the board dispatched it

events.name: plan-finds-nothing-to-do
events.doc: The planner established the work is already merged, so there is nothing to build. A clean terminal rather than a failure — and reopenable, because it is a judgement and a person may overrule it. The ticket-review gate posts it too: its own verdict marker classifies under the backlog stage and would leave the card reading as planning-in-progress, so a stop verdict posts the planning stage's terminal marker alongside it.

events.name: planning-failed
events.where: board_failure.go
events.doc: The planning stage itself failed — a spent retry budget, an agent that died without a verdict. Distinct from the planner concluding there is nothing to do, which is a terminal rather than a fault and must never be reddened as one.

events.name: start-fix-run
events.where: board_transition.go ApplyFix
events.doc: Dropping a bug on Fix. The run is self-planning — it produces its own plan rather than requiring one.

events.name: preflight-clear
events.doc: Preflight found no question that only a human can answer, so the run proceeds to reproduce the report. Everything the evidence could settle, it settled.

events.name: preflight-asks
events.doc: The one place the pipeline asks a question, asked up front rather than halfway through.

events.name: triage-verdict-confirmed
events.doc: Triage reproduced the report, so the run continues as a confirmed bug and plans its fix. A not-a-bug or undetermined verdict goes to the skeptic instead of ending the run.

events.name: triage-verdict-no-bug
events.doc: A no-fix verdict is never acted on directly — it must survive a challenge first.

events.name: challenge-upholds
events.doc: The skeptic could not refute the not-a-bug or undetermined verdict, so it stands and the run ends without a code change. The challenge runs once — a verdict that survives it is not re-challenged.

events.name: challenge-refutes
events.doc: The skeptic reproduced it. The run continues as a confirmed bug, using the skeptic's reproduction. Runs once — never loops back through triage.

events.name: fix-plan-written
events.doc: The self-planning fix run wrote its own plan and starts carrying it out. It plans for itself because it entered from a bug report rather than from a planned ticket, so there is no attached plan to execute.

events.name: fix-written
events.doc: A regression test that fails first, then the change that makes it pass. Verification is a separate step so the fails-before/passes-after evidence is produced by something other than the code that wrote the fix.

events.name: verify-not-done
events.guard: under the retry budget; only a failure that reproduced charges an attempt
events.doc: The verify gate found the fix wanting and the run loops back inside itself. No marker records it: [human:bug-verify] is evidence, not a transition, so nothing on the ticket distinguishes this from the fix still running. The item genuinely moves; the record does not.

events.name: fix-budget-spent
events.doc: The fix could not be made to verify within the run's budget. The item stops for a human rather than shipping a change nothing proved.

events.name: start-implementation
events.where: board_transition.go launchForwardStage / isReworkTransition / isBuildRetry
events.doc: The plan-executing path. From reviewed it is the rework loop — a failing review verdict sends the item back to be rebuilt with the findings.

events.name: handoff-posted
events.where: posted via `human handoff post`, which verifies the commits are reachable on the branch first
events.doc: Branch and commits are recorded on the ticket for whoever reviews next. The commits are verified reachable on the branch before the marker is posted, so a handoff never names work nobody else can see.

events.name: implementation-failed
events.where: board_failure.go
events.doc: The daemon's failure watcher classifies an agent that exited without posting its handoff. It fires for the implementation stage as a whole — failedHeaderFor(BoardImplementation) knows the stage, never which phase the run had reached — so every state of the stage leads here.

events.name: start-review
events.where: board_failure.go chainReviewAfterCleanBuild; board_reconcile.go if that hook was lost
events.doc: Automatic: a clean build whose handoff names a reachable branch flows straight into its review. A board fix run instead runs the review inline in its own container and the daemon launches no second one.

events.name: review-verdict
events.doc: Pass and fail are the same marker and the same state — the verdict rides in a field. Whether that verdict BLOCKS is decided once, by daemon.VerdictFailed, and shipped to the board as verdictFailed; the board never re-tests the string. A blocking verdict keeps the item out of Deploy and offers the rework gesture instead.

events.name: review-failed
events.doc: The review stage itself failed — a binding gate such as a missing branch or unreachable commits — not a failing verdict.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_failure.go — the failure watcher, via failedHeaderFor(BoardVerification)

events.name: start-deploy
events.where: internal/marker/marker.go — the only thing left that knows this marker; no pipeline code posts it
events.guard: the review verdict must not be failing
events.doc: Dropping on Deploy, the pre-loop way. Nothing in the pipeline posts deploy-started any more — the Done stage fronts the merge with the PR review loop (start-pr-review) and records pr-review-started instead. The marker stays a valid one to post by hand, and the board still reads it as Done/Running, so the edge is real but nobody automatic walks it. The corpus agrees: the one history carrying deploy-started is also the one carrying no pr-review marker at all.

events.name: pr-opened
events.doc: The pull request is opened as a draft, so a half-reviewed change is not mergeable by anyone.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop, PRActionReview

events.name: pr-changes-requested
events.doc: The fixer commits to the LOCAL branch and never pushes, so the reviewer reads the new commit rather than a stale pushed head.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop, PRActionFix

events.name: pr-refixed
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop, PRActionReview — the same action, re-entered after a fix round
events.doc: The reviewer re-reads the branch after the fixer's commit. It is the same review step rather than a different one, so what bounds the loop is the round count, not a separate escalating transition.

events.name: pr-review-passed
events.where: board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop
events.doc: The reviewer approved. The draft is un-drafted and the item goes to the CI gate. Recorded as a marker like every other outcome of the loop — success used to be the only transition here that left no trace, so a reader could not tell an approved review whose merge is running from a review still in flight. It also retires the loop sub-phase, so the badge stops reading 'PR review…' through the CI gate, rebase and merge.

events.name: pr-loop-escalates
events.doc: Budget spent, unreviewable, or an outcome it cannot parse. It never merges on a state it cannot read.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop — prEscalationReason names which of the three it was

events.name: ci-red
events.doc: A red-but-mechanical failure dispatches the fixer instead of failing the item. A cancelled check counts as no answer yet, not as a no.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go deployFailedOrDispatchFixer — ciFailureFixable decides fixer or stop

events.name: ci-regated
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvanceDeployFix — publishes the fixer's branch, then re-enters DeployBranch
events.doc: The fixer's container holds no push credentials, so its deliverable is the local branch and the daemon publishes it before re-entering the gate. Publishing first is what makes the resolution count at all: the gate reads the branch from origin, so an unpublished fix would be silently discarded and the same failure re-hit.

events.name: ci-green-merged
events.doc: If the base moved on, the branch is rebased and CI re-gated on the new head before merging. Past the merge, branch cleanup and closing the ticket are best-effort and never fail the item. A branch already merged into the base is the same outcome reached without a PR at all: the engine records it and stops, which is why the merge is reachable directly from deploying.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go DeployBranch — one engine, entered from the board and from `human deploy` (cmd/cmddeploy/deploy.go RunDeploy)

events.name: deploy-failed
events.doc: The deploy gave up. The marker names the condition that is blocking — for a deploy-fixer escalation it quotes the failure the fixer was dispatched to fix, which for CI names the red checks — and it does not offer a gesture that cannot work: where re-running Deploy would hit the same failure, it says so instead of advising the retry.
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go deployFailed, and AdvanceDeployFix for a fixer that did not converge

events.name: stage-asks
events.where: board_state.go pauseOnOpenOptions
events.doc: A stage found a genuine fork and stopped. The item is not working and not dead — it is waiting on a person, and reads as decision-needed rather than running.

events.name: decision-made
events.where: board_state.go optionChosenQueued
events.doc: A human picked an answer; the run relaunches with the choice in hand. dst is the stage the block NAMES, not the stage the item sits in — planning is the common case. A PR-loop escalation deliberately names implementation even though the item is in the deploy stage: the fixer raised a question only a code change can answer, so the choice rebuilds, and the rebuild re-adopts the still-open draft PR. The item pauses correctly meanwhile, because an open block pauses every card whose own stage ranks at or after the one named.

events.name: substrate-unreachable
events.where: board_retry.go ExitOutage
events.doc: One marker per stage. It costs no retry budget and the reconcile pass relaunches it each interval until the substrate returns.

events.name: launch-refused-no-plan
events.where: board_transition.go refuseIfUnplanned
events.doc: The plan executor was launched on a ticket with no plan, so the launch is refused before any agent claims it. The item surfaces back at planning where a human can start one. A relaunch attempted on a card that already failed meets the same gate, so the refusal is also a move a stopped card makes onto itself: the plan is still missing, and the card stays exactly as red as it was.

events.name: source-unreadable
events.where: internal/board/gate.go PMRoleNotice; internal/board/compose.go
events.doc: The tracker instance failed to load — an unreachable credential store, a config error. Every item it carries becomes unobservable at once, so this is a property of the fetch rather than of any one ticket. It resolves by itself when the source is reachable again; nothing about the item changed.

events.name: source-readable-again
events.where: internal/board/compose.go — the next fetch that resolves a PM-role result
events.doc: The source came back and the item's real state is re-derived from its markers — it returns to whatever they say, not to `filed`. The single dst here is a topological placeholder: this machine has one destination per transition and the true one is computed. Nothing about the item changed while it was unobservable.

events.name: reopen-planning
events.where: board_transition.go reopenResolved; desktop App.Reopen
events.doc: A person judged the nothing-to-do terminal wrong and re-plans. Separate from every retry gesture because the automatic relaunch drives the identical same-stage request — only an explicitly human call may re-run a clean terminal.

events.name: reopen-fix
events.where: board_transition.go reopenResolved — classifyFixPipeline routes to ApplyFix/ApplySecurityFix
events.doc: A person judged the no-fix-needed verdict wrong. The card re-enters its OWN self-planning pipeline, so it re-triages from the top rather than being handed to the plan executor, which would refuse it for having no plan.

events.name: legacy-pr-opened
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: The PR-opening lifecycle that predates the deploy pipeline. Still classified so threads written before deploy markers existed keep deriving; nothing posts it today.

events.name: legacy-pr-pushed
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: Legacy: the PR was opened. It classifies as the done stage's DONE state — the same state the merge produces — so on an old thread an opened PR renders where a shipped one does. Recognized for those threads only.

events.name: legacy-pr-failed
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: Legacy: opening the PR failed. Recognized for pre-deploy-pipeline threads only.

events.name: gate-opens-planning
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go planPrompt — every planning dispatch runs /human-ticket-review as its first phase
events.doc: The ordinary path into the gate, and it moves nothing. The daemon posts planning-started when it dispatches and the gate is the first thing that dispatch runs, so the gate marker arrives AFTER the planning marker — and the card keeps reading as planning, because furthest-stage-wins ranks the planning marker above the gate's backlog-stage one. The gate is a PHASE of planning here, not a stage the item leaves planning for: the same run carries straight on into planning's own work, and planning's markers keep arriving as if the gate had never been a place.
events.prompt: human-ticket-reviewer-agent.md — the gate posts its own ticket-review-started marker

events.name: start-pr-review
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go runDoneStage — the Done stage opens the draft PR and launches the reviewer; isDeployRetry re-enters it on a card whose deploy already failed
events.doc: Dropping on Done. The stage fronts the deploy with the PR review loop rather than posting deploy-started and merging, so the item enters the loop directly and deploying is never recorded on this path. Re-dropping a failed card is the same move, which is why stopped is a source: without it a conflicted deploy would be a dead end escapable only by re-implementing already-reviewed work (SC-735).

events.name: redeploy-after-outage
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go isDeployRetry — an outage card at the Done stage is relaunched in place exactly like a failed one, so the reconcile backoff can re-drive it (SC-2307)
events.doc: The same re-entry as start-pr-review, made by the machine rather than by a person: an infrastructure failure is not the ticket's fault, so nobody should have to drag the card back. Split from start-pr-review because the actor differs, and a state's who_may_act is checked against the transitions that leave it.

events.name: gate-verdict-in-planning
events.where: internal/claude/embed/human-ticket-reviewer-agent.md
events.doc: The gate's verdict inside a planning dispatch. It records why, and deliberately does not end the stage — a stop verdict posts planning's own terminal marker alongside it, and ready/reframed simply carry on. Both are why the verdict moves nothing here.

events.name: pr-fix-asks
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go escalatePRLoop — a fixer that ends needing input becomes a decision rather than a red card
events.doc: The PR fixer hit something only a person can settle. Unlike every other stage-asks, the daemon raises this one rather than the agent: the fixer records its need on exit and the loop turns that into the block, naming the implementation stage so choosing rebuilds through the normal chain and re-adopts the still-open draft PR.

ownership.doc: Which machine may fire a transition. A stage is stamped with the daemon that posted its deciding marker (BoardCard.StageDaemonID, from the marker's machine: field).
rules: The machine acting on its own initiative — the reconcile takeover pass — refuses a stage another daemon stamped: WorkGate.ownedHereOrUnowned in internal/daemon/board_reconcile_gate.go. An unstamped stage (single-daemon, or a thread written before stamping) is takeable by anyone.
A human gesture is NOT restricted by ownership. Racing a live foreign run is prevented instead by idempotency: a running card refuses every drop (isDuplicateDrop), whichever machine started it.

Ownership is carried to the board as stageDaemonId so a reader can tell a stage owned elsewhere from an unowned one. It is the missing input for liveness across machines: no agent running HERE means dead only if this machine owns the stage.

progress.doc: How an item shows that it is moving. Each in-container phase writes stage.<name> to `human state` with a timestamp — preflight, triage, challenge, fix, verify, review, pr-review, pr-fix, deploy-fix — and the board reads the newest one onto a running card as `activity`.
progress.why: Between implementation-started and ready-for-review an item passes through six phases that all render as one unchanging word. That word is identical at thirty seconds, at fourteen hours, and when the agent behind it is dead, so nothing on the card distinguishes progress from a hang. The phase changing is the signal; its not changing is the other one.
progress.note: Read for running cards only, and never invented: a run that recorded no phase shows the stage word exactly as before.

invariants.doc: What each state guarantees while an item sits in it. The transition table says how an item MOVES; these four fields say what is true when it does not, which is the question the pipeline's stuck-card bugs kept turning out to be.

fields.holds: What must be true of the item while it is in this state.
fields.who_may_act: Which declared actors can move it out. An empty list is a true terminal.
fields.stale_when: What makes the state suspect rather than merely slow.
fields.if_nothing_happens: What the machine does on its own when nobody acts — the answer a planner needs and the one a transition table cannot hold.

constants.BoardReconcileInterval: 2m, jittered ±50% — how often the durable pass re-scans open cards (internal/daemon/board_reconcile.go)
constants.StuckRunningGrace: 15m — how long a running card is left alone before liveness is judged
constants.DefaultStageRetries: 2 — automatic in-place relaunches of one stage (internal/daemon/board_retry.go)
constants.DefaultPRReviewRounds: 3 — review→fix rounds before the loop escalates (internal/daemon/pr_review_loop.go)
constants.OutageWaitBound: 6h — how long an outage may be relaunched before it is handed to a person (internal/daemon/board_outage.go)

stage_defaults.doc: The liveness rule for a RUNNING stage, stated once. A state naming one of these in `inherits` takes its stale_when and if_nothing_happens from here, and `note` adds what is true of that state alone. Once rather than per state because it IS one rule: seven copies would need seven coordinated edits to stay true, which is the drift this document exists to prevent — reproduced inside it.

planning.stale_when: It has sat past StuckRunningGrace (15 minutes) and no agent for (key, planning) is alive on the machine that owns the stage — or one is alive but has recorded no new phase, which the reconcile pass stops before redding.
planning.if_nothing_happens: The durable reconcile pass (every ~2 minutes) posts [human:planning-failed] and relaunches in place, up to DefaultStageRetries (2). A machine-chosen silence stop does not charge that budget.

implementation.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace with no live agent for (key, implementation).
implementation.if_nothing_happens: The reconcile pass posts [human:implementation-failed] and relaunches in place, up to DefaultStageRetries (2).

verification.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace with no live agent for (key, verification).
verification.if_nothing_happens: The reconcile pass posts [human:review-failed] and relaunches in place, up to DefaultStageRetries (2).

done.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace with no live agent for (key, done).
done.if_nothing_happens: The reconcile pass posts [human:deploy-failed] and relaunches in place, up to DefaultStageRetries (2).

pr-loop.stale_when: No loop half-agent alive on this machine. The generic stuck-running pass deliberately SKIPS a loop card (doneStageLoopActive), so a loop is recovered by re-driving rather than by redding.
pr-loop.if_nothing_happens: reconcilePRLoops re-reads the recorded state and advances or escalates, idempotently. Bounded by DefaultPRReviewRounds (3); past it the loop escalates rather than merging on a state it cannot read.
